chunks: Hadith 506 — Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام came to a people who had been struck by a calamity, and he said:
"May Allah mend your weakness, grant you a good consolation, and have mercy on your deceased."

key_terms.جَبَرَ: may He restore, mend, or strengthen after brokenness
key_terms.مُتَوَفَّاكُمْ: your deceased one, the person who has passed away
key_terms.مُصِيبَةٍ: a calamity or affliction, here referring to bereavement
key_terms.وَهْنَكُمْ: your weakness or frailty caused by grief

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام say when consoling people after a death?
ai.summary: This hadith records words of taʿziyah spoken by Imam Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام to people afflicted by bereavement. It teaches compassionate condolence through du'a for strength, consolation, and mercy for the deceased.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.506 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) visited a group of people who had experienced a loss and said:
"May Allah (swt) strengthen you in your weakness, grant you beautiful patience, and have mercy on your deceased."
